problems.description: Committed vendored dependency type declarations (cache.d.ts, index.d.ts from gray-matter/marked) into the repo tree. These account for 3026 of 3026 convention violations and ~most of the +4027 lines. They belong in node_modules and should be gitignored, not tracked.
No .gitignore for node_modules/ or dist/ in this greenfield commit, which is what allowed generated .d.ts files to land in the diff.
Diff is scaffolding only (jest config, lockfile, generated typings, +6 functions); no actual source module, so architectural structure of the SSG is not yet established.

strengths: jest.config.js is correctly scoped to tests/ with ts-jest preset and standard testMatch, following conventional ts-jest setup.
package-lock.json committed, enabling reproducible dependency resolution.
Dependency set is lean and appropriate for a static site generator (gray-matter, marked, yargs).
commit_reviews.summary: Clean, conventional greenfield scaffold (ts-jest config + committed lockfile) undercut by committing generated node_modules .d.ts files, which are the sole driver of the 0.46 convention score and the bulk of the line count.

problems.description: Adds @types/handlebars@^4.1.0, a deprecated stub types package — the package-lock entry itself states 'handlebars provides its own type definitions, so you do not need this installed.' This is an unnecessary, already-deprecated dependency that adds noise to package.json/lockfile and creates dependency-confusion surface.

Mechanical convention score of 0.46 (3026 violations) is misleading: all listed violations are in generated dependency declaration files (cache.d.ts, index.d.ts), none in agent-authored code — the measured low score is pre-existing dependency noise, not this commit.

The refactor flips hardcoded HTML builders into a TemplateEngine abstraction plus a layout/template frontmatter mechanism in one commit; behavior-contracting (e.g., date formatting changed to explicit 'en-US' locale) rides along with the architectural change, making the intent harder to review.

strengths: Extracts inline HTML generation into a dedicated TemplateEngine, improving separation of concerns and cutting cognitive complexity by 10 (SonarQube delta)
Zero new bugs and zero added duplication per SonarQube measurements
New --templates CLI option follows the existing yargs option pattern (type/default/describe) exactly, matching src/index.ts conventions
Refactor is contained: parsePage/frontmatter extended cleanly with template/layout fields while keeping the existing build() entry point signature-compatible
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound refactor that replaces hardcoded HTML with a reusable template engine (bugs +0, complexity -10), but the deprecated stub @types/handlebars dependency is technical debt, and the low measured convention score is an artifact of generated .d.ts files rather than this commit's code.

problems.description: Path traversal in serve(): filePath = path.join(outputDir, req.url) resolves request-controlled paths outside ./dist (e.g. GET /../package.json), serving arbitrary files; should normalize and verify the resolved path stays within outputDir.
serve.ts adds an untested surface (MIME mapping, live-reload injection, rebuild-on-change) with no new jest tests; the story prompt only required existing tests to keep passing.

No graceful shutdown: the http server, WebSocketServer, and chokidar watcher are never closed on SIGINT, leaving watchers/handles open; ServeInstance exposes the handles but nothing wires them to a close path.
Synchronous fs calls (existsSync/statSync/readFileSync) run in the request handler and block the event loop on every request; acceptable for a dev server but heavier than needed.
injectLiveReload does a naive replace of the first '</body>' occurrence and falls back to appending, which misbehaves if the script tag already exists or the page has no closing body tag.

The 0.46 convention score is dragged entirely by generated declaration files (cache.d.ts, index.d.ts) that are NOT part of this diff; the commit's own code follows naming conventions correctly (PascalCase ServeOptions/ServeInstance, camelCase functions, UPPER_CASE MIME_TYPES).

strengths: serve command mirrors the existing build command's yargs option pattern (defaults + describe) and reuses build() from ssg.ts, keeping build logic single-source.
Correct dependency placement: ws/chokidar in dependencies, @types/ws in devDependencies, with package-lock.json updated consistently.
SonarQube delta is positive: bugs 0, smells -14, cognitive complexity -11, duplications -7.7%.
demandCommand error message updated to advertise the new serve command.
Implements the full Session 3 spec: chokidar watching, ws live-reload injection, --port option, serving from ./dist.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid integration commit that fits the existing yargs/ssg architecture and fulfills the Session 3 spec, though the low 0.46 convention score is a measurement artifact of generated .d.ts files outside this diff and the real gaps are an unguarded outputDir path, missing tests, and no lifecycle cleanup.

problems.description: DevServerPlugin exposes setEngine/start/getInstance outside the Plugin interface, so the lifecycle-hook contract doesn't uniformly describe plugin behavior; engine coupling happens through a side channel rather than the hook context.
rebuild() in dev-server-plugin.ts swallows all build errors with an empty catch (// nop), hiding failures from the live-reload workflow.
BuildContext uses a [key: string]: any index signature, weakening type safety in an otherwise typed refactor.
TemplatePlugin writes output files directly to disk in onFile/afterBuild and hardcodes 'My Static Site' as the index title, mixing rendering concerns into plugin code and baking in a magic default.
Adds runtime dependencies (ws, chokidar, gray-matter, marked); diff is truncated so package.json declaration could not be verified.

strengths: Clean lifecycle-hook plugin interface (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) is a genuinely extensible refactor target.
Reuses existing types (Page, PageTemplateData, TemplateEngine) instead of duplicating them across plugins.
Mechanical deltas are strongly positive: -4 smells, -46 cognitive complexity, -2.1% duplication, 0 new bugs.
Dev-server plugin cleanly separates HTTP serving, live-reload websocket fan-out, and file watching.
commit_reviews.summary: Net-positive refactor that extracts a sensible plugin abstraction and cuts complexity/smells, though it introduces minor debt via loose BuildContext typing, a silent error catch, and plugin methods that dodge the stated interface.

problems.description: CacheManager is a god-class mixing five concerns (manifest persistence, page caching, dirty-checking, file/template hashing, build stats) with 6 parallel structures — manifest plus pageCache, htmlCache, frontmatterCache, _pageEntries — storing the same frontmatter/html/renderedHTML data twice, matching the measured cognitive complexity +179 and 1.8% duplication

Data is stored redundantly in both the serialized manifest and in-memory Maps, so mutations must be kept in sync across save()/buildManifest()/set* paths; buildManifest() silently drops any page missing one of frontmatter/page/renderedHTML with no error surfaced
setPageEntry(slug, sourceHash, templateName, layoutName) is a 4-positional-argument setter — an options object would be less fragile

Build stats (pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped) require external callers to call incrementBuilt()/incrementSkipped() manually, coupling build logic to cache internals instead of deriving stats from actual work done
Inconsistent defensive copying: setCachedPage and setCachedFrontmatter clone their inputs while setCachedHTML stores raw references — asymmetric mutation semantics across the three setters

Mechanical convention score 0.46 with 3026 violations, but every enumerated violation is in generated .d.ts files (cache.d.ts, index.d.ts) — the metric likely overstates problems in hand-written code; discrepancy flagged

computeFileHash re-reads and md5-hashes every source file and computeTemplatesHash walks the whole template dir on each build, partially eroding the incremental-build win (render cost, not IO cost, is what is skipped)

strengths: Adds a genuinely useful incremental-build capability exposed via clean --incremental and --clean CLI flags with a serializable cache manifest
Reuses the existing Page/Frontmatter type system and integrates through the build/plugin context rather than introducing parallel types
Defensive on IO: corrupt cache manifests are caught and ignored on load, and delete() fully resets all state
No new bugs per SonarQube; 0 bugs in the delta
commit_reviews.summary: A working incremental-build cache landed cleanly at the CLI/plugin seams, but its value is undercut by a monolithic CacheManager holding duplicated parallel state (+179 cognitive complexity, +6 smells, 1.8% duplication), with the low convention score largely driven by generated .d.ts files rather than hand-written code.

compounding_issues: Committed node_modules/, dist/, and package-lock in Session 1 (5,153 files changed), making every later commit carry massive diff noise and bloating git history

Session 1's hardcoded HTML string templates were entirely replaced by Handlebars in Session 2, and its monolithic functions were decomposed in Session 4's plugin refactor — the early rendering code was largely throwaway

The dev-server plugin was never registered in the engine's plugin pipeline (serve.ts instantiates it standalone and injects the engine), so rebuilds bypass its lifecycle hooks — an inconsistency carried from Session 4 into Session 5

Session 5 introduced a type-unsafe `_fromCache` marker flag on Page (`(page as any)._fromCache`) shared across markdown-plugin, ssg.ts, and template-plugin, creating hidden cross-cutting coupling between the cache layer and plugins
key_decisions: Adopting Handlebars with layouts, partials, and default templates in Session 2, which became the rendering backbone every later feature (dev server, plugins, cache) hooked into
Refactoring to a plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) in Session 4, which let Session 5 add incremental caching as a clean cross-cutting feature
Building the dev server with WebSocket live-reload and chokidar watching in Session 3, later folded into a dev-server plugin
Implementing incremental builds via MD5 content hashing plus template-directory hashing persisted in a .ssg-cache.json manifest in Session 5
Migrating from monolithic module-level build() functions to an SSGEngine class in Session 4, improving testability and extensibility
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 produced a functional but monolithic generator with hardcoded HTML and a single source file; Session 2 upgraded it with a proper templating layer and grew tests from 7 to 16; Session 3 integrated a real dev server (tests to 25); Session 4 was the turning point, restructuring into a plugin architecture while preserving all existing behavior with no regressions; Session 5 built the most sophisticated feature — incremental caching with template/content hashing — on top of that plugin seam, adding 19 new tests (44 total) and wiring --incremental/--clean into the CLI. All sessions exited successfully with tests passing and no recovery cascade. Minor smells (the _fromCache type-unsafe flag and the unregistered dev-server plugin) indicate the architecture was strained slightly at the edges, but the overall arc is clearly improving in both design quality and test coverage.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-layered progression where each session's prompt builds naturally on the prior commit and quality improves throughout, held back only by early repository bloat (committed node_modules) and a couple of architectural seams that never fully closed.
